crime_highlights: D.W. told Mr. Walkus that he was not welcome in her apartment and should leave
Mr. Walkus nevertheless forced open the door and entered D.W.'s apartment without her permission
he forced her into her bedroom
D.W. struggled and yelled for help
Mr. Walkus removed D.W.'s clothing and pinned her onto her bed
rationale_highlights: I accept the conclusions set out in the Gladue report
Mr. Walkus' father was physically and sexually abused at St. Michael's Indian Residential School
Because of the mitigating factors that are present, particularly those identified in Mr. Walkus' Gladue report
I will account for Mr. Walkus' mitigating factors when considering where the length of his custodial sentence should fall
note: Conclusion is that mitigation shapes length within range.

crime_highlights: Mr. Telechea jumped on Sergeant Singh's back
Mr. Telechea grabbed the baton with both hands and, starting with his hands over his head, began beating Sergeant Singh in the area of his head
Mr. Telechea struck Sergeant Singh three to four times with the baton
Mr. Telechea's actions were explosive, extremely violent, and sustained
He recounted that he feared for his life on that day
rationale_highlights: Mr. Telechea and his family and community have experienced many of the identified Gladue factors
The Gladue principles require restraint in sentencing Indigenous offenders
I find that Mr. Telechea's circumstances are tied to his offending behaviour, and at least partially attenuate his moral culpability
Mr. Telechea's reliance on intoxicants is directly tied to his dysfunctional life from the time he was a child, which itself is directly tied to the Gladue factors I have outlined
